title: The Afternoon Brief: Injuries mount across NFL; LIV faces vendor crisis as Saudi funding ends
dek: The afternoon brings compounding injury news in football and the first concrete evidence of LIV Golf's financial strain as contractors report unpaid invoices and the Saudi funding closure arrives this month. Institutional transitions also crystallize: Mourinho returns to Madrid, Bhatia's consortium gains control of Liverpool, and the Premier League moves toward referee accountability.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Two distinct crises are unfolding in parallel: NFL teams face cascading injuries to key offensive weapons weeks before the season starts, while LIV Golf enters an acute liquidity moment with vendors uncompensated and no confirmed new capital commitment.
bottom_line: The midday picture crystallizes two distinct institutional moments: NFL and MLB teams face cascading injuries that will test roster depth in the season's opening weeks, while LIV Golf enters an acute liquidity crisis with documented unpaid vendor invoices and no confirmed timeline for new capital. In football governance, Infantino's path to re-election narrows as four major federations withdraw support and a legal challenge to his eligibility awaits committee review. Watch whether BC Partners closes its funding commitment before vendor claims escalate into court filings, whether injured players' timelines hold as teams enter preseason, and whether FIFA's governance committee rules on Infantino's eligibility before the 2027 election cycle formally begins.
body: The injury toll across professional football has deepened through the afternoon. The Cubs confirmed Dansby Swanson's Grade 2 oblique strain will sideline him four to six weeks, a timeline that could eliminate the shortstop from the remainder of the regular season and upend Chicago's NL Central chase. In the NFL, the Jets' Breece Hall strained his right groin in practice Monday and will miss 2-3 weeks but is expected to be ready for the Sept. 13 opener against Tennessee, per coach Aaron Glenn. Meanwhile, the Saints' Jordyn Tyson, the No. 8 overall draft pick, sustained a right hamstring injury during a joint practice with Jacksonville on Thursday and could miss two months, per NFL Network sources, a timeline that would sideline him through at least Week 6 of the regular season. All three injuries occurred without contact or in controlled settings, underscoring how fragile the preseason window is for teams attempting to build momentum.

LIV Golf's financial crisis has moved from speculation into documented vendor complaint. A second report confirms contractors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands to nearly $100,000, with minimal response from the league's accounts receivable and legal teams as the Saudi Public Investment Fund halts funding this month. Mobii Systems Group Limited, a Canadian streaming-technology vendor, claims LIV owes it more than $1.1 million for breach of contract and unpaid invoices. One unnamed contractor stated: "There's no response from the accounts receivable department. Even their legal counsel has not responded to demand letters." This pattern of silence stands in contrast to CEO Scott O'Neill's public statements this month expressing appreciation for PIF's patience as the league pursues new investors. The convergence of unpaid vendor invoices, termination notices to contractors, restructuring executives on the board, and the WARN Act filing suggests LIV faces acute liquidity pressure. Full-time employees have not reported missed paychecks, but the withholding of contractor payments raises immediate questions about cash availability if BC Partners' investment commitment is delayed or incomplete.

Away from crisis management, institutional transitions are formalizing. José Mourinho was officially unveiled as Real Madrid manager on Tuesday with a three-year contract, returning to the club for the first time as head coach since 2013. He told Real Madrid TV the return is both professional and emotional: "It's like coming home. Emotionally, it's more beautiful than the first time I came." The squad includes six new signings ahead of Saturday's opener against Espanyol. In English football, the 1892 Holdings consortium, led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia and including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, acquired approximately 38 percent of Liverpool FC from Fenway Sports Group in a deal that values the club between £5bn and £6bn, per BBC Sport. Bhatia will become vice-chairman pending regulatory approval. The consortium holds an option to purchase a controlling stake within 12 months, meaning the structure of Liverpool's ownership could fundamentally change within a year. The Premier League also announced it will publish full verdicts from its Key Match Incidents Panel on referee and VAR decisions for the first time this season, ending a policy of private judgment and moving toward public accountability on contentious calls.

In governance, Gianni Infantino faces isolation on multiple fronts. The Scottish Football Association announced it will not vote for Infantino's 2027 re-election, joining England, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland and aligning Scotland with UEFA's 55 member associations, which have threatened a boycott of all FIFA competitions. Scottish FA chief executive Ian Maxwell cited governance failures and lack of transparency. An advocacy group has challenged Infantino's legal eligibility to run for a fourth term, and the FIFA governance committee's response to that ineligibility request will determine whether institutional defection translates into a legal barrier to his candidacy.

The afternoon also brought commemorations. Bill Rasmussen, who founded ESPN and launched the world's first 24-hour sports television network on Sept. 7, 1979, died Tuesday at 93 from complications of Parkinson's disease. O.J. Brigance, the Baltimore Ravens' longtime player engagement adviser and Super Bowl champion linebacker, died Sunday at 56 after a 19-year battle with ALS that far exceeded his initial 2-5 year prognosis. He recorded the Ravens' first tackle in their Super Bowl XXXV championship victory in January 2001 and founded the Brigance Brigade Foundation, which continues his legacy in player mentorship.

In golf, Scottie Scheffler, the world's top-ranked player, won the FedEx St. Jude Championship by eight shots at TPC Southwind to open the FedEx Cup Playoffs. The margin established commanding form heading into the playoff sequence. In Australian football, the AFL Tribunal upheld Jacob van Rooyen's three-match suspension for a striking incident that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, rejecting Melbourne's appeal and the club's biomechanist evidence. Van Rooyen will miss Saturday's game against the Western Bulldogs and the Demons' first two finals.
